units.zh: 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝，姓劉氏，初名知遠，其先沙陀部人也，其後世居於太原。
units.en: Gaozu, posthumous name the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor, was of the Liu clan and originally named Zhiyuan. His forebears were Shatuo; his family later settled at Taiyuan.
units.literal: Gaozu, the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor—surname Liu, originally named Zhiyuan—his ancestors were of the Shatuo tribe; later generations dwelt at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 知遠弱不好弄，嚴重寡言，面紫色，目多白睛，凜如也。
units.en: As a boy Zhiyuan shunned childish games. Grave and sparing of speech, with a purple cast to his face and prominent whites in his eyes, he had a chilling presence.
units.literal: From youth Zhiyuan disliked play; grave and taciturn, his face was purple and his eyes showed much white—he seemed stern and forbidding.

units.zh: 與晉高祖俱事明宗為偏將，明宗及梁人戰德勝，晉高祖馬甲斷，梁兵幾及，知遠以所乘馬授之，復取高祖馬殿而還，高祖德之。
units.en: He and Gaozu of Jin served Mingzong as subordinate commanders. At Desheng, Gaozu’s horse armor broke and Liang soldiers nearly reached him; Zhiyuan gave Gaozu his own mount, then took Gaozu’s horse and guarded the rear. Gaozu was grateful.
units.literal: He served Mingzong together with Gaozu of Jin as subordinate generals. When Mingzong fought the Liang at Desheng, Gaozu of Jin’s horse armor broke and Liang troops nearly reached him; Zhiyuan gave him the horse he was riding, then took Gaozu’s horse and covered the rear as they returned, and Gaozu was grateful to him.

units.zh: 高祖留守北京，知遠為押衙。
units.en: When Gaozu held the Northern Capital, Zhiyuan was his chief adjutant.
units.literal: When Gaozu stayed behind to guard the Northern Capital, Zhiyuan served as chief adjutant.

units.zh: 潞王從珂反，愍帝出奔，高祖自鎮州朝京師，遇愍帝于衞州，止傳舍，知遠遣勇士石敢袖鐵槌侍高祖以虞變。
units.en: When Prince Congke of Lu rebelled and Mindi fled, Gaozu came from Zhenzhou toward the capital and met Mindi at Weizhou, where they stopped at the courier lodge. Zhiyuan sent the warrior Shi Gan to wait on Gaozu with an iron mallet hidden in his sleeve in case matters turned dangerous.
units.literal: When Congke, Prince of Lu, rebelled and Mindi fled, Gaozu came from Zhenzhou to court at the capital, met Mindi at Weizhou, and stopped at the courier lodge. Zhiyuan sent the brave man Shi Gan to hide an iron mallet in his sleeve and attend Gaozu in case of trouble.

units.zh: 高祖與愍帝議事未決，左右欲兵之，知遠擁高祖入室，敢與左右格鬬而死，知遠即率兵盡殺愍帝左右，留帝傳舍而去。
units.en: When Gaozu and Mindi could not settle matters, the emperor’s attendants moved to seize Gaozu. Zhiyuan bundled Gaozu into an inner room. Shi Gan fought the attendants and died, and Zhiyuan then led troops in, killed all of Mindi’s attendants, left the emperor at the lodge, and went away.
units.literal: Gaozu and Mindi discussed affairs without reaching a decision, and the attendants wanted to use force against him. Zhiyuan embraced Gaozu and took him into a room; Gan fought with the attendants and died, and Zhiyuan immediately led troops to kill all of Mindi’s attendants, left the emperor at the courier lodge, and departed.

units.zh: 廢帝入立，高祖復鎮河東，已而有隙，高祖將舉兵，知遠與桑維翰密為高祖謀畫，贊成之。
units.en: After the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Gaozu returned to Hedong. A rift soon opened; when Gaozu prepared to raise troops, Zhiyuan and Sang Weihan secretly planned for him and helped make the revolt happen.
units.literal: After the Deposed Emperor entered and took the throne, Gaozu again governed Hedong. Before long there was a rift, and when Gaozu was about to raise troops, Zhiyuan and Sang Weihan secretly made plans for Gaozu and helped bring it about.

units.zh: 高祖即位於太原，以知遠為侍衞親軍都虞候，領保義軍節度使。
units.en: When Gaozu proclaimed himself emperor at Taiyuan, he appointed Zhiyuan chief aide of the Palace Guard and military governor of Baoyi.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne at Taiyuan, he made Zhiyuan chief aide of the Palace Guard and acting military governor of Baoyi.

units.zh: 契丹耶律德光送高祖至潞州，臨決，指知遠曰：「此都軍甚操剌」，世俗謂勇猛為「操剌」，錄其本語，「無大故勿棄之。」
units.en: Yelü Deguang of the Khitan escorted Gaozu to Luzhou. As they parted, he pointed at Zhiyuan and said, “This commander is very caola”; common speech used caola for bravery, and the text preserves the original word; “Do not abandon him without serious cause.”
units.literal: The Khitan Yelü Deguang escorted Gaozu to Luzhou, and at parting pointed to Zhiyuan and said, “This commander is very caola”; in common speech bravery was called “caola,” and the original wording is recorded; “Do not abandon him without a major reason.”

units.zh: 天福二年，遷侍衛馬步軍都指揮使，領忠武軍節度使。
units.en: In the second Tianfu year he became commander of the palace horse-and-foot guards and military commissioner of Zhongwu.
units.literal: In the second Tianfu year he was transferred to commander of the palace horse-and-foot guards and made military commissioner of Zhongwu.

units.zh: 已而以杜重威代知遠領忠武，徙知遠領歸德，知遠恥與重威同制，杜門不出。
units.en: Du Chongwei soon took over Zhongwu in his place and Zhiyuan was shifted to Guide. He was shamed to hold equal rank with Chongwei and refused to leave his residence.
units.literal: Soon after, Du Chongwei replaced Zhiyuan in Zhongwu; Zhiyuan was moved to Guide. Ashamed to share the same rank as Chongwei, he shut his gates and would not go out.

units.zh: 高祖怒，欲罷其兵職，宰相趙瑩以為不可，高祖乃遣端明殿學士和凝就第宣諭，知遠乃受命。
units.en: Jin Gaozu, furious, meant to remove him from command, but Chancellor Zhao Ying dissuaded him. He Ning of the Duanming Hall was sent to Zhiyuan’s home to read the imperial reassurance, and only then did Zhiyuan take up his duties again.
units.literal: Gaozu was angry and wished to strip him of his military post; Chancellor Zhao Ying said it could not be done. Gaozu then sent Duanming Hall academician He Ning to his house to proclaim the imperial will, and Zhiyuan then accepted the order.

units.zh: 五年，徙鄴都留守。
units.en: In the fifth year he was made regent of Yedu.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to regent of Yedu.

units.zh: 九月，朝京師，高祖幸其第。
units.en: In the ninth month he came to court, and Jin Gaozu called at his house.
units.literal: In the ninth month he went to the capital; Gaozu visited his residence.

units.zh: 六年，拜河東節度使、北京留守。
units.en: In the sixth year he received Hedong and the Northern Capital regency.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed military commissioner of Hedong and regent of the Northern Capital.

units.zh: 七年，高祖崩。
units.en: In the seventh year Jin Gaozu died.
units.literal: In the seventh year Gaozu died.

units.zh: 知遠從高祖起太原，有佐命功，自出帝立，與契丹絕盟，用兵北方，常疑知遠勛位已高，幸晉多故而有異志，每優尊之。
units.en: Zhiyuan had stood with Jin Gaozu from the founding at Taiyuan and earned his place among the founders. After the Outgoing Emperor broke with the Khitan and warred in the north, the court often feared that Zhiyuan’s honors had outgrown his loyalty and that Jin’s calamities might tempt him elsewhere—yet he was lavished with ever greater favor.
units.literal: Zhiyuan had followed Gaozu from the rise at Taiyuan and had merit in founding the dynasty. From the time the Outgoing Emperor took the throne, broke the Khitan alliance, and campaigned in the north, he often suspected that Zhiyuan’s achievements and rank were already high and that, with Jin beset by troubles, he harbored a different ambition—yet each time he treated him with exceptional honor.

units.zh: 拜中書令，封太原王、幽州道行營招討使，又拜北面行營都統。
units.en: He was made Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Taiyuan, then campaign repression commissioner for Youzhou and, later, overall commander of the northern field army.
units.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed Prince of Taiyuan, made campaign repression commissioner on the Youzhou circuit, and later overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters.

units.zh: 開運二年四月，封北平王，三年五月，加守太尉，然王未嘗出兵。
units.en: In the fourth month of Kaiyun 2 he became Prince of Beiping; in the fifth month of the third year he was named Defender Grand Marshal. He never led an army in person.
units.literal: In the fourth month of Kaiyun 2 he was enfeoffed Prince of Beiping; in the fifth month of year 3 he was made Defender Grand Marshal—yet the prince never took the field.

units.zh: 契丹寇澶州，別遣偉王攻雁門，敗之於秀容。
units.en: When the Khitan struck Cangzhou they also sent the Great King against Yanmen; Zhiyuan routed him at Xiurong.
units.literal: The Khitan raided Cangzhou and separately sent the Great King against Yanmen; he was defeated at Xiurong.

units.zh: 八月，殺吐渾白承福等族，取其貲鉅萬，良馬數千。
units.en: In the eighth month he exterminated the Tuguhun leader Bai Chengfu and his kin, seizing vast stores of goods and thousands of fine horses.
units.literal: In the eighth month he killed the Tuguhun Bai Chengfu and his clan, taking their wealth in the tens of thousands and fine horses by the thousand.

units.zh: 四年，契丹犯京師，出帝北遷，王遣牙將王峻奉表契丹，耶律德光呼之為兒，賜以木拐一，木拐，虜法貴之如中國几杖，非優大臣不可得。
units.en: In the fourth year the Khitan seized the capital and the Outgoing Emperor was taken north. The prince sent Wang Jun, a staff officer, to present tribute to the Khitan. Yelü Deguang addressed him as a son and gave him a wooden staff—in Khitan usage as honored as a Chinese seat and cane, and granted only to ministers in highest favor.
units.literal: In the fourth year the Khitan took the capital and the Outgoing Emperor was moved north. The prince sent teeth officer Wang Jun with a memorial to the Khitan; Yelü Deguang called him “son” and granted one wooden staff—a wooden staff, in barbarian custom, is prized as the Chinese prize a seat and staff; only favored great ministers could receive it.

units.zh: 峻持拐歸，虜人望之皆避道。
units.en: Jun returned with the staff, and Khitan along the way stepped aside at the sight of it.
units.literal: Jun carried the staff back; Khitan who saw it all yielded the road.

units.zh: 峻還，為王言契丹必不能有中國，乃議建國。
units.en: Back at Taiyuan, Jun reported that the Khitan could not long keep the Central Plains, and they began to plan a new dynasty.
units.literal: When Jun returned he told the prince that the Khitan surely could not hold China, and they then discussed founding a state.

units.zh: 二月戊辰，河東行軍司馬張彥威等上箋勸進。
units.en: On wuchen in the second month Zhang Yanwei, deputy to the Hedong campaign staff, and others presented a memorial urging accession.
units.literal: On wuchen of the second month, Hedong campaign deputy Zhang Yanwei and others submitted a memorial urging him to take the throne.

units.zh: 辛未，皇帝即位，稱天福十二年。
units.en: On xinwei Liu Zhiyuan took the throne and kept the era name at the twelfth Tianfu year.
units.literal: On xinwei the emperor ascended the throne and called the era the twelfth Tianfu year.

units.zh: 磁州賊首梁暉取相州來歸。
units.en: Liang Hui, a rebel leader in Cizhou, took Xiang prefecture and submitted.
units.literal: Liang Hui, bandit chief of Cizhou, seized Xiangzhou and came to submit.

units.zh: 變來降曰「來歸」，哀斯人也。
units.en: The text changes “came to surrender” to “came home” out of pity for these people.
units.literal: Changing “came to surrender” to “came home” is to pity these people.

units.zh: 是時天下無主，得其主則往歸之，與乎叛于彼而來於此者異矣。
units.en: At the time the realm had no master. When people found one, they went over to him; that was different from defecting from one side to another.
units.literal: At this time the realm had no ruler; when they found their ruler, they went and returned to him, which differs from rebelling from one side and coming to another.

units.zh: 漢高祖非有德之君，惶惶斯人之無所歸者，猶得而歸也，故曰「歸」。
units.en: Gaozu of Han was no virtuous ruler, yet anxious people with no one to turn to could still find him and return; therefore the text says “returned.”
units.literal: Gaozu of Han was not a ruler possessed of virtue, but these anxious people with nowhere to turn still found someone to return to; therefore it says “returned.”

units.zh: 武節都指揮使史弘肇取代州，殺其刺史王暉。
units.en: Shi Hongzhao of the military inspectorate seized Dai prefecture and executed the prefect Wang Hui.
units.literal: Military inspector Shi Hongzhao took Dai prefecture and killed its prefect Wang Hui.

units.zh: 晉州將藥可儔殺守將駱從朗及括錢使、諫議大夫趙熙來歸。
units.en: Yao Ketal, a Jinzhou officer, killed the garrison commander Luo Conglang, the tax-enforcement commissioner, and remonstrance grandee Zhao Xi, then submitted the prefecture.
units.literal: Jinzhou general Yao Ketal killed garrison commander Luo Conglang, the money-levying commissioner, and remonstrance grandee Zhao Xi, and came to submit.

units.zh: 辛巳，陜州留後趙暉、潞州留後王守恩來歸。
units.en: On xinsi Zhao Hui, regent of Shanzhou, and Wang Shouen, regent of Luzhou, submitted.
units.literal: On xinsi, Shanzhou regent Zhao Hui and Luzhou regent Wang Shouen came to submit.

units.zh: 三月丙戌朔，蠲河東雜稅。
units.en: On the bingxu new moon of the third month miscellaneous levies in Hedong were abolished.
units.literal: On bingxu, the new moon of the third month, miscellaneous taxes in Hedong were remitted.

units.zh: 辛卯，延州軍亂，逐其節度使周密。
units.en: On xinmao troops at Yanzhou rebelled and expelled Military Commissioner Zhou Mi.
units.literal: On xinmao the Yanzhou army mutinied and drove out its military commissioner Zhou Mi.

units.zh: 壬辰，丹州指揮使高彥詢以其州來歸。
units.en: On renchen Gao Yanxun, commander of Danzhou, brought his prefecture over.
units.literal: On renchen, Danzhou commander Gao Yanxun submitted his prefecture.

units.zh: 壬寅，契丹遯，聞漢起太原，畏而去，故與自去異其文，「遯」者，退避之稱。
units.en: On renyin the Khitan withdrew. Since they left out of fear after hearing that Han had risen at Taiyuan, the wording differs from ordinary departure: “dun” means a retreat or withdrawal.
units.literal: On renyin, the Khitan withdrew. They heard that Han had risen at Taiyuan, were afraid, and left; therefore the wording differs from simply leaving on their own. “dun” is a term for retreating to avoid danger.

units.zh: 以其將蕭翰為宣武軍節度使守汴州。
units.en: They left their general Xiao Han as military governor of Xuanwu to hold Bianzhou.
units.literal: They made their general Xiao Han military governor of Xuanwu to guard Bianzhou.

units.zh: 夏四月己未，右都押衙楊邠為樞密使，蕃漢兵馬都孔目官郭威權樞密副使。
units.en: On jiwei in the fourth month Yang Bin, right chief adjutant, became Privy Councilor, and Guo Wei, chief clerk for Fan and Han horse troops, acting Vice Privy Councilor.
units.literal: In the fourth month, summer, on jiwei, Right Chief Adjutant Yang Bin was made Privy Councilor and Fan-Han horse-and-foot chief clerk Guo Wei acting Vice Privy Councilor.

units.zh: 契丹陷相州，殺梁暉。
units.en: The Khitan took Xiang prefecture and killed Liang Hui.
units.literal: The Khitan captured Xiangzhou and killed Liang Hui.

units.zh: 癸亥，立魏國夫人李氏為皇后。
units.en: On guihai Lady Li of Wei was made empress.
units.literal: On guihai Lady Li of Wei was established as empress.

units.zh: 甲子，河東節度判官蘇逢吉、觀察推官蘇禹珪為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: On jiazi Su Fengji, military judge of Hedong, and Su Yugui, observation push official, became Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilors.
units.literal: On jiazi, Hedong military judge Su Fengji and observation push official Su Yugui were made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilors.

units.zh: 乙丑，侍衛親軍步軍都指揮使史弘肇取潞州。
units.en: On yichou Shi Hongzhao, commander of the Imperial Guard foot corps, seized Luzhou.
units.literal: On yichou, Imperial Guard foot commander Shi Hongzhao took Luzhou.

units.zh: 戊辰，奉國指揮使武行德以河陽來歸。
units.en: On wuchen Wu Xingde of Fengguo brought Heyang over.
units.literal: On wuchen, Fengguo commander Wu Xingde submitted Heyang.

units.zh: 史弘肇取澤州。
units.en: Shi Hongzhao took Ze prefecture.
units.literal: Shi Hongzhao took Ze prefecture.

units.zh: 丙子，契丹耶律德光卒於欒城，契丹入於鎮州。
units.en: On bingzi Yelü Deguang died at Luancheng, and the Khitan fell back on Zhenzhou.
units.literal: On bingzi Yelü Deguang died at Luancheng; the Khitan entered Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 五月甲午，太原尹劉崇為北京留守。
units.en: On jiawu in the fifth month Liu Chong, magistrate of Taiyuan, was named regent of the Northern Capital.
units.literal: On jiawu of the fifth month, Taiyuan Magistrate Liu Chong was made regent of the Northern Capital.

units.zh: 丙申，如東京。
units.en: On bingshen the emperor set out for the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: On bingshen he proceeded to the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 蕭翰遁歸於契丹，以郇國公李從益知南朝軍國事。
units.en: Xiao Han fled to the Khitan and installed Li Congyi, Duke of Xun, to manage the Southern Court’s armies and administration.
units.literal: Xiao Han fled back to the Khitan and made Li Congyi, Duke of Xun, oversee military and state affairs of the Southern Court.

units.zh: 戊申，次絳州，刺史李從朗來歸。
units.en: On wushen the court paused at Jiang prefecture, where Prefect Li Conglang submitted.
units.literal: On wushen he halted at Jiang prefecture; Prefect Li Conglang submitted.

units.zh: 六月丙辰，次河陽，殺李從益及其母於京師。
units.en: On bingchen of the sixth month the march stopped at Heyang while Li Congyi and his mother were executed in the capital.
units.literal: On bingchen of the sixth month he halted at Heyang; Li Congyi and his mother were put to death at the capital.

units.zh: 甲子，至自太原。
units.en: On jiazi the emperor entered the capital from Taiyuan.
units.literal: On jiazi he arrived, having come from Taiyuan.

units.zh: 戊辰，改國號漢，高祖初建國無國號，蓋其制詔皆無明文，故闕不書。
units.en: On wuchen the state name was changed to Han. When Gaozu first founded the regime, it apparently had no declared dynastic name; the edicts gave no clear wording, so the text omitted it.
units.literal: On wuchen, the state name was changed to Han. When Gaozu first founded the state, it had no state name; likely the edicts and rescripts all lacked explicit wording, so it was omitted and not written.

units.zh: 然稱天福十二年，則國仍號晉可知，但無明據，故慎於所疑爾。
units.en: Since the year was still called Tianfu 12, the state evidently still used the Jin name, but without explicit proof the text is cautious about the doubtful point.
units.literal: Yet since it called the year Tianfu 12, one can know that the state still called itself Jin, but because there was no clear evidence, it was cautious about what was doubtful.

units.zh: 此書「改國號漢」，則未改之前宜有所稱，此可以推知也。
units.en: Because this entry says “changed the state name to Han,” there must have been some prior designation; that much can be inferred.
units.literal: Since here it writes “changed the state name to Han,” before the change there must have been something it was called; this can be inferred.

units.zh: 赦罪人、蠲民稅。
units.en: Criminals were pardoned, and taxes on the people were remitted.
units.literal: Criminals were pardoned and the people’s taxes were remitted.

units.zh: 于闐遣使者來。
units.en: Envoys arrived from Khotan.
units.literal: Khotan sent envoys.

units.zh: 是夏，劉昫薨。
units.en: That summer Liu Xu died.
units.literal: That summer Liu Xu died.

units.zh: 秋閏七月乙丑，禁造契丹服器。
units.en: On yichou in the intercalary seventh month the court forbade the manufacture of Khitan garments and gear.
units.literal: In the intercalary seventh month of autumn, on yichou, making Khitan dress and vessels was forbidden.

units.zh: 天雄軍節度使杜重威反，杜重威於晉出帝時避出帝名去「重」，至漢而復之。
units.en: Du Chongwei, military governor of Tianxiong, rebelled. Under the Later Jin Deposed Emperor he had dropped the character “Chong” to avoid the emperor’s name; under Han he restored it.
units.literal: Du Chongwei, military governor of Tianxiong, rebelled. During the time of the Later Jin Deposed Emperor, Du Chongwei avoided the emperor’s name by dropping “Chong,” and when Han came he restored it.

units.zh: 天平軍節度使高行周為鄴都行營都部署以討之。
units.en: Gao Xingzhou of Tianping was appointed overall commander of the Yedu campaign to attack him.
units.literal: Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Tianping, was made overall commander of the Yedu field headquarters to campaign against him.

units.zh: 庚辰，追尊祖考為皇帝，妣為皇后：高祖湍謚曰明元，廟號文祖，祖妣李氏謚曰明貞；
units.en: On gengchen forebears were raised posthumously—emperors and their consorts empresses: great-great-grandfather Tuan received the temple name Wenzu and posthumous title Mingyuan; his consort Lady Li, Mingzhen;
units.literal: On gengchen the emperor’s forebears were posthumously honored as emperors and their consorts as empresses: great-grandfather Tuan, posthumous name Mingyuan, temple name Wenzu; great-grandmother Lady Li, posthumous name Mingzhen;

units.zh: 曾祖昂謚曰恭僖，廟號德祖，祖妣楊氏謚曰恭惠；
units.en: great-grandfather Ang, Dezu and Gongxi; his consort Lady Yang, Gonghui;
units.literal: great-great-grandfather Ang, posthumous name Gongxi, temple name Dezu; his consort Lady Yang, posthumous name Gonghui;

units.zh: 祖僎謚曰昭憲，廟號翼祖，祖妣李氏謚曰昭穆；
units.en: grandfather Juan, Yizu and Zhaoxian; his consort Lady Li, Zhaomu;
units.literal: grandfather Juan, posthumous name Zhaoxian, temple name Yizu; his consort Lady Li, posthumous name Zhaomu;

units.zh: 考典謚曰章聖，廟號顯祖，妣安氏謚曰章懿。
units.en: father Dian, Xianzu and Zhangsheng; mother Lady An, Zhangyi.
units.literal: father Dian, posthumous name Zhangsheng, temple name Xianzu; mother Lady An, posthumous name Zhangyi.

units.zh: 以漢高皇帝為高祖，光武皇帝為世祖，皆不祧。
units.en: The Han Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Guangwu were enshrined as the dynasty’s Gaozu and Shizu, neither displaced from the ancestral line.
units.literal: Han’s Emperor Gaozu was taken as dynastic Gaozu and Guangwu as dynastic Shizu—neither was removed from the temple line.

units.zh: 八月，護聖指揮使白再榮逐契丹，以鎮州來歸。
units.en: In the eighth month Bai Zairong of Husheng expelled the Khitan and brought Zhen prefecture over.
units.literal: In the eighth month, Husheng commander Bai Zairong drove out the Khitan and submitted Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 丙申，安國軍節度使薛懷讓殺契丹之將劉鐸，入於邢州。
units.en: On bingshen Xue Huairang of Anguo killed the Khitan commander Liu Duo and took Xing prefecture.
units.literal: On bingshen, Anguo military commissioner Xue Huairang killed the Khitan general Liu Duo and entered Xingzhou.

units.zh: 九月甲戌，吏部尚書竇貞固守司空兼門下侍郎，翰林學士、中書舍人李濤為中書侍郎：同中書門下平章事。
units.en: On jiaxu Dou Zhengu of the Ministry of Personnel kept the Ministry of Works and the Vice Directorship of the Secretariat; Li Tao, Hanlin academician and drafting officer, became Vice Director—both Associate Grand Councilors.
units.literal: On jiaxu, Minister of Personnel Dou Zhengu continued as Minister of Works and Vice Director of the Secretariat; Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafting officer Li Tao was made Vice Director of the Secretariat: both Associate Grand Councilors.

units.zh: 庚辰，北征。
units.en: On gengchen the emperor marched north.
units.literal: On gengchen the northern campaign set out.

units.zh: 冬十月甲申，次韋城，赦河北。
units.en: On jiashen in the tenth month the army encamped at Weicheng and proclaimed an amnesty for Hebei.
units.literal: On jiashen of the tenth month, winter, the court halted at Weicheng and amnestied Hebei.

units.zh: 十一月壬申，杜重威降。
units.en: On renshen of the eleventh month Du Chongwei surrendered.
units.literal: On renshen of the eleventh month Du Chongwei surrendered.

units.zh: 十二月癸巳，至自鄴都。
units.en: On guisi the emperor came back from Yedu.
units.literal: On guisi he returned from Yedu.

units.zh: 乾祐元年春正月乙卯，大赦，改元。
units.en: On yimao in the first month of Qianyou 1 the court proclaimed a great amnesty and changed the era name.
units.literal: On yimao, first month of spring in Qianyou 1, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed.

units.zh: 己未，更名暠。
units.en: On jiwei Gaozu took the taboo name Gao.
units.literal: On jiwei he was renamed Gao.

units.zh: 丁丑，皇帝崩於萬歲殿。
units.en: On dingchou the emperor died in the Hall of Myriad Years.
units.literal: On dingchou the emperor died in the Hall of Myriad Years.

units.zh: 年五十四。
units.en: He was fifty-four.
units.literal: He was fifty-four years old.

units.zh: 隱帝，高祖第二子承祐也。
units.en: Yindi was Gaozu’s second son, Chengyou.
units.literal: Yindi was Gaozu’s second son, Chengyou.

units.zh: 高祖即位，拜右衞上將軍、大內都點檢。
units.en: After Gaozu took the throne, Chengyou was appointed Senior General of the Right Guard and inspector-general of the inner palace.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Chengyou was appointed Senior General of the Right Guard and Inspector-general of the Inner Palace.

units.zh: 魏王承訓長而賢。
units.en: Chengxun, Prince of Wei, was older and capable.
units.literal: Chengxun, Prince of Wei, was older and worthy.

units.zh: 高祖愛之，方屬以為嗣，承訓薨，高祖不豫，悲哀疾劇，乃以承祐屬諸將相。
units.en: Gaozu loved him and intended to make him heir, but Chengxun died. Gaozu fell ill, grief worsened the sickness, and he entrusted Chengyou to the generals and ministers.
units.literal: Gaozu loved him and was just about to entrust the succession to him when Chengxun died. Gaozu fell ill, and his grief made the illness severe; he then entrusted Chengyou to the generals and ministers.

units.zh: 宰相蘇逢吉曰：「皇子承祐未封王，請亟封之。」
units.en: Chancellor Su Fengji said, “The imperial son Chengyou has not yet been made a prince. Please enfeoff him immediately.”
units.literal: The chancellor Su Fengji said, “The imperial son Chengyou has not yet been enfeoffed as prince; please enfeoff him at once.”

units.zh: 未及封而高祖崩，祕不發喪，殺杜重威。
units.en: Before the enfeoffment could happen, Gaozu died. The court concealed the mourning and killed Du Chongwei.
units.literal: Before he could be enfeoffed, Gaozu died; they kept the mourning secret and did not announce it, and killed Du Chongwei.

units.zh: 乾祐元年二月辛巳，封承祐周王。
units.en: On xinsi in the second month of Qianyou 1 Chengyou was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhou.
units.literal: On xinsi of the second month of Qianyou 1, Chengyou was enfeoffed Prince of Zhou.

units.zh: 是日，皇帝即位於柩前。
units.en: That same day the Hidden Emperor took the throne before the bier.
units.literal: That day the emperor ascended the throne before the coffin.

units.zh: 壬辰，右衛大將軍、鳳翔巡檢使王景崇及蜀人戰於大散關，敗之。
units.en: On renchen Wang Jingchong, senior general of the Right Guard and Fengxiang inspection commissioner, met the Shu at Dasanguan and routed them.
units.literal: On renchen, Right Guard senior general and Fengxiang inspection commissioner Wang Jingchong fought the Shu at Dasanguan and defeated them.

units.zh: 癸巳，大赦。
units.en: On guisi the court proclaimed a great amnesty.
units.literal: On guisi a great amnesty was proclaimed.

units.zh: 三月壬戌，竇貞固為大行皇帝山陵使，吏部侍郎段希堯為副，太常卿張昭為禮儀使，兵部侍郎盧價為鹵簿使，御史中丞邊蔚為儀仗使。
units.en: On renxu Dou Zhengu directed the late emperor’s tomb works, with Duan Xiyao of the Ministry of Personnel as deputy; Zhang Zhao oversaw the rites, Lu Jia the procession, and Censor-in-Chief Bian Wei the honor guard.
units.literal: On renxu, Dou Zhengu was made director for the late emperor’s tomb, Vice Minister of Personnel Duan Xiyao deputy, Director of Ceremonies Zhang Zhao ritual commissioner, Vice Minister of War Lu Jia escort commissioner, and Censor-in-Chief Bian Wei arms commissioner.

units.zh: 丁丑，李濤罷。
units.en: On dingchou Li Tao left office.
units.literal: On dingchou Li Tao was dismissed.

units.zh: 護國軍節度使李守貞反，陷潼關。
units.en: Li Shouzhen, military commissioner of Huguo, rebelled and took Tong Pass.
units.literal: Huguo military commissioner Li Shouzhen rebelled and seized Tong Pass.

units.zh: 夏四月辛巳，陜州兵馬都監王玉克潼關。
units.en: On xinsi in the fourth month Wang Yu, Shanzhou’s horse-and-foot inspector, recovered Tong Pass.
units.literal: On xinsi of the fourth month, summer, Shanzhou horse-and-foot inspector Wang Yu took Tong Pass.

units.zh: 壬午，永興軍將趙思綰叛附於李守貞，客省使王峻帥師屯於關西。
units.en: On renwu Zhao Sizhen of Yongxing mutinied to Li Shouzhen’s side, and Wang Jun, guest commissioner, encamped with an army west of the Pass.
units.literal: On renwu, Yongxing officer Zhao Sizhen rebelled and joined Li Shouzhen; guest commissioner Wang Jun led troops stationed west of the Pass.

units.zh: 峻不命為將，又不令討賊，但令以兵實關西，下文乃見命將。
units.en: Wang Jun was not made a commander or ordered to attack the rebels; he was only told to reinforce Guanzhong. The appointment of commanders appears later.
units.literal: Jun was not appointed a general, nor was he ordered to attack the rebels; he was only ordered to fill Guanzhong with troops, and the appointment of generals appears below.

units.zh: 楊邠為中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事，郭威為樞密使，鎮寧軍節度使郭從義為永興軍兵馬都部署。
units.en: Yang Bin became Vice Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Personnel, Associate Grand Councilor; Guo Wei, Privy Councilor; and Guo Congyi of Zhenning, deployment commissioner for Yongxing horse and foot.
units.literal: Yang Bin was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of Personnel, Associate Grand Councilor; Guo Wei became Privy Councilor; Zhenning military commissioner Guo Congyi was made Yongxing horse-and-foot deployment commissioner.

units.zh: 戊子，保義軍節度使白文珂為河中兵馬都部署。
units.en: On wuzi Bai Wenke of Baoyi was named overall deployment commissioner for the Hezhong armies.
units.literal: On wuzi, Baoyi military commissioner Bai Wenke was made overall deployment commissioner for Hezhong horse and foot.

units.zh: 河決原武。
units.en: The Yellow River burst its dikes at Yuanwu.
units.literal: The Yellow River broke its banks at Yuanwu.

units.zh: 五月己未，回鶻遣使者來。
units.en: On jiwei in the fifth month envoys came from the Uyghurs.
units.literal: On jiwei of the fifth month Uyghur envoys arrived.

units.zh: 乙亥，魏州內黃民武進妻一產三男子。
units.en: On yihai the wife of Wu Jin of Neihuang in Weizhou gave birth to triplet sons.
units.literal: On yihai, the wife of Wu Jin of Neihuang in Weizhou bore three sons in one birth.

units.zh: 河決滑州魚池。
units.en: The Yellow River burst its dikes at Yuchi in Huazhou.
units.literal: The Yellow River broke its banks at Yuchi in Huazhou.

units.zh: 旱，蝗。
units.en: Drought struck, and locusts swarmed.
units.literal: Drought; locusts.

units.zh: 秋七月戊申朔，彰德軍節度使王繼弘殺其判官張易。
units.en: On the wushen new moon of the seventh month Wang Jihong, military commissioner of Zhangde, killed his administrative judge Zhang Yi.
units.literal: On wushen, new moon of the seventh month, autumn, Zhangde military commissioner Wang Jihong killed his judge Zhang Yi.

units.zh: 翙鵒食蝗。
units.en: Sacred ibises devoured the locusts.
units.literal: Sacred ibises ate the locusts.

units.zh: 丙辰，禁捕翙鵒。
units.en: On bingchen the court forbade the taking of sacred ibises.
units.literal: On bingchen the hunting of sacred ibises was forbidden.

units.zh: 庚申，郭威同中書門下平章事。
units.en: On gengshen Guo Wei was made Associate Grand Councilor.
units.literal: On gengshen Guo Wei became Associate Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 癸亥，契丹鄚州刺史王彥徽來奔。
units.en: On guihai Wang Yanhui, Khitan prefect of Mo, defected to Han.
units.literal: On guihai Wang Yanhui, prefect of Mo in Khitan territory, came over in flight.

units.zh: 庚午，殺成德軍副使張鵬。
units.en: On gengwu Zhang Peng, deputy commissioner of Chengde, was put to death.
units.literal: On gengwu Zhang Peng, deputy commissioner of Chengde, was executed.

units.zh: 乙亥，王景崇叛附於李守貞。
units.en: On yihai Wang Jingchong turned rebel and went over to Li Shouzhen.
units.literal: On yihai Wang Jingchong rebelled and joined Li Shouzhen.

units.zh: 八月壬午，郭威討李守貞。
units.en: On renwu in the eighth month Guo Wei marched to suppress Li Shouzhen.
units.literal: On renwu of the eighth month Guo Wei campaigned against Li Shouzhen.

units.zh: 九月，西面行營都虞候尚弘遷及趙思綰戰，敗績。
units.en: In the ninth month Shang Hongqian, deputy of the Western Campaign, met Zhao Sizhen and suffered defeat.
units.literal: In the ninth month, Western Campaign deputy commander Shang Hongqian fought Zhao Sizhen and was defeated.

units.zh: 冬十月甲申，吐蕃使斯漫篤蘭氈藥斯來。
units.en: On jiashen in the tenth month a Tibetan mission led by Simandulan Zhan Yaosi arrived.
units.literal: On jiashen of the tenth month, winter, the Tibetan envoy Simandulan Zhan Yaosi came.

units.zh: 十一月甲寅，殺太子太傅李崧，滅其族。
units.en: On jiayin Li Song, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was executed and his entire clan wiped out.
units.literal: On jiayin of the eleventh month Li Song, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was executed and his clan exterminated.

units.zh: 壬申，葬睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝於睿陵。
units.en: On renshen Gaozu, the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor, was laid to rest at Ruiling.
units.literal: On renshen the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor was buried at Ruiling.

units.zh: 在河南告成縣。
units.en: It was in Gaocheng county, Henan.
units.literal: It was in Gaocheng county, Henan.

units.zh: 十二月己卯，彰武軍節度使高允權殺太子太師致仕劉景巖。
units.en: On jimao Gao Yunquan of Zhangwu murdered Liu Jingyan, the retired Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: On jimao of the twelfth month, Zhangwu military commissioner Gao Yunquan killed the retired Grand Preceptor Liu Jingyan.

units.zh: 二年隱帝即位至此，宜改元而不改元，具周顯德二年注。
units.en: From Yindi’s accession in year 2 down to here, the reign title should have been changed but was not; the full note appears under Zhou Xiande 2.
units.literal: From Yindi’s accession in year 2 to this point, the reign title ought to have been changed but was not; this is fully noted under Zhou Xiande 2.

units.zh: 而帝名承祐，年名乾祐，舉國臣民共稱而不改避，當時莫大之失，本紀無譏者，但書其實，後世自見也。
units.en: The emperor’s personal name was Chengyou, while the reign title was Qianyou; the entire realm used it without alteration or avoidance, an enormous fault at the time. The Basic Annals do not comment, but by recording the facts let later readers see it.
units.literal: Moreover, the emperor’s name was Chengyou and the reign name was Qianyou; the whole state, ministers and people alike, used it without changing or avoiding it, which was the greatest error of the time. The Basic Annals do not criticize it, but only write the facts, so later generations will see it for themselves.

units.zh: 春正月乙巳朔，赦囚。
units.en: On the yisi new moon of the first month, prisoners were pardoned.
units.literal: In spring, first month, on the yisi new moon, prisoners were pardoned.

units.zh: 二月丙子，蠲民紐配租。
units.en: On bingzi supplemental cloth levies on the people were abolished.
units.literal: On bingzi the people’s supplementary cloth levies were remitted.

units.zh: 夏五月，李守貞之將周光遜降。
units.en: In the fifth month Zhou Guangxun, an officer under Li Shouzhen, surrendered.
units.literal: In the fifth month of summer, Zhou Guangxun, a general of Li Shouzhen, surrendered.

units.zh: 乙丑，趙思綰降。
units.en: On yichou Zhao Sizhen surrendered.
units.literal: On yichou Zhao Sizhen surrendered.

units.zh: 六月辛卯，回鶻首領楊彥珣來。
units.en: On xinmao in the sixth month the Uyghur chieftain Yang Yanxun arrived.
units.literal: On xinmao of the sixth month, Uyghur chieftain Yang Yanxun came.

units.zh: 西涼府遣使者來。
units.en: Envoys arrived from the Western Liang prefectural administration.
units.literal: The Western Liang prefectural seat sent envoys.

units.zh: 蝗。
units.en: Locusts swarmed.
units.literal: Locusts.

units.zh: 秋七月丁巳，郭威殺華州留後趙思綰於京兆。
units.en: On dingsi in the seventh month of autumn Guo Wei executed Zhao Sizhen, rear commander of Huazhou, at Jingzhao.
units.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on dingsi, Guo Wei killed Zhao Sizhen, rear commander of Huazhou, at Jingzhao.

units.zh: 甲子，克河中。
units.en: On jiazi Hezhong fell.
units.literal: On jiazi Hezhong was taken.

units.zh: 守貞自焚死，故不書伏誅。
units.en: Because Shouzhen burned himself to death, the text does not say he was executed.
units.literal: Shouzhen burned himself to death; therefore it does not write that he was executed.

units.zh: 八月，郭從義殺前永興巡檢喬守溫。
units.en: In the eighth month Guo Congyi put to death Qiao Shouwen, the former Yongxing inspector.
units.literal: In the eighth month Guo Congyi killed Qiao Shouwen, former inspector of Yongxing.

units.zh: 丙戌，郭威使來獻俘。
units.en: On bingxu an envoy from Guo Wei arrived with prisoners for the court.
units.literal: On bingxu Guo Wei’s envoy came presenting captives.

units.zh: 冬十月，契丹寇趙、魏，群臣進添都馬。
units.en: In the tenth month Khitan forces struck Zhao and Wei prefectures, and the ministers offered extra horses for the capital guard.
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter the Khitan raided Zhao and Wei; the ministers presented additional capital horses.

units.zh: 契丹陷內丘。
units.en: The Khitan seized Neiqiu.
units.literal: The Khitan took Neiqiu.

units.zh: 己丑，郭威及宣徽南院使王峻伐契丹。
units.en: On jichou Guo Wei marched against the Khitan with Wang Jun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
units.literal: On jichou Guo Wei and Wang Jun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, campaigned against the Khitan.

units.zh: 十一月，契丹遯。
units.en: In the eleventh month the Khitan pulled back.
units.literal: In the eleventh month the Khitan withdrew.

units.zh: 三年春正月，西面行營都部署趙暉克鳳翔。
units.en: In the third year, in the first month of spring, Zhao Hui, overall commander of the western field army, captured Fengxiang.
units.literal: In the third year, spring, in the first month Zhao Hui, overall deployment commander of the Western Campaign, took Fengxiang.

units.zh: 景崇自焚死，故不書伏誅。
units.en: Because Jingchong burned himself to death, the text does not say he was executed.
units.literal: Jingchong burned himself to death; therefore it does not write that he was executed.

units.zh: 丙午，郭威進添都馬。
units.en: On bingwu Guo Wei offered extra horses for the capital guard.
units.literal: On bingwu Guo Wei presented additional capital horses.

units.zh: 壬子，趙暉獻馘俘。
units.en: On renzi Zhao Hui presented heads and prisoners taken in battle.
units.literal: On renzi Zhao Hui presented severed heads and captives.

units.zh: 二月甲戌，旌表潁州汝陰民麹溫門閭。
units.en: On jiaxu of the second month the court honored the household gate of Qu Wen of Ruyin in Ying prefecture for exemplary conduct.
units.literal: On jiaxu of the second month the household gate of Qu Wen, a commoner of Ruyin in Ying prefecture, was marked with honor.

units.zh: 三月己酉，寒食，望祭於南禦園。
units.en: On jiyou of the third month, on Cold Food Day, the emperor made offering by gazing toward the Southern Imperial Garden.
units.literal: On jiyou of the third month, on Cold Food Day, he performed look-toward sacrifice at the Southern Imperial Garden.

units.zh: 夏四月壬午，郭威以樞密使為天雄軍節度使。
units.en: On renwu in the fourth month Guo Wei, Privy Councilor, was appointed military commissioner of Tianxiong.
units.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on renwu, Guo Wei the Privy Councilor was made military commissioner of Tianxiong.

units.zh: 六月癸卯，河決原武。
units.en: On guimao in the sixth month the Yellow River burst its dikes at Yuanwu.
units.literal: On guimao in the sixth month the river broke at Yuanwu.

units.zh: 秋八月，達靼來附。
units.en: In the eighth month the Dadan tribes came over in submission.
units.literal: In the eighth month of autumn the Dadan submitted.

units.zh: 冬十一月丙子，殺楊邠及侍衛親軍都指揮使史弘肇、三司使王章，皆滅其族。
units.en: On bingzi in the eleventh month Yang Bin was executed, along with Shi Hongzhao, commander of the palace guards, and Wang Zhang, commissioner of the Three Departments; every clan of the three was wiped out.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on bingzi, Yang Bin was killed, together with Shi Hongzhao, commander of the palace personal army, and Wang Zhang, commissioner of the Three Departments—all their clans were exterminated.

units.zh: 郭威反。
units.en: Guo Wei rose in rebellion.
units.literal: Guo Wei rebelled.

units.zh: 庚辰，義成軍節度使宋延渥叛附於威。
units.en: On gengchen Song Yanwo of Yicheng turned rebel and went over to Guo Wei.
units.literal: On gengchen Song Yanwo, military commissioner of Yicheng, rebelled and joined Guo Wei.

units.zh: 壬午，威犯封丘，泰寧軍節度使慕容彥超軍於七里店。
units.en: On renwu Guo Wei advanced on Fengqiu while Murong Yanchao of Taining drew up his army at Qilidian.
units.literal: On renwu Guo Wei attacked Fengqiu; Murong Yanchao, military commissioner of Taining, encamped at Qilidian.

units.zh: 癸未，勞軍於北郊。
units.en: On guiwei the emperor reviewed the army in the northern suburbs.
units.literal: On guiwei the emperor reviewed troops at the northern suburbs.

units.zh: 甲申，勞軍於劉子陂。
units.en: On jiashen he reviewed the army again at Liuzipo.
units.literal: On jiashen he reviewed troops at Liuzipo.

units.zh: 慕容彥超及郭威戰，敗績，開封尹侯益叛降於威。
units.en: Murong Yanchao met Guo Wei in battle and was routed; Hou Yi, governor of Kaifeng, defected to the rebel side.
units.literal: Murong Yanchao fought Guo Wei and was defeated; Hou Yi, governor of Kaifeng, rebelled and surrendered to Guo Wei.

units.zh: 郭允明反。
units.en: Guo Yunming rose in rebellion.
units.literal: Guo Yunming rebelled.

units.zh: 乙酉，皇帝崩，年二十。
units.en: On yiyou the emperor died at the age of twenty.
units.literal: On yiyou, the emperor died; he was twenty years old.

units.zh: 周廣順元年葬之許州陽翟縣，號潁陵，為賊所葬，故不書。
units.en: In Zhou Guangshun 1 he was buried at Yangzhai county in Xuzhou and the tomb was called Yingling. Because rebels buried him, the text does not record it.
units.literal: In Zhou Guangshun 1 he was buried in Yangzhai county, Xuzhou; it was named Yingling, but because he was buried by rebels, it is not written.

units.zh: 蘇逢吉自殺。
units.en: Su Fengji took his own life.
units.literal: Su Fengji killed himself.

units.zh: 漢亡。
units.en: Han fell.
units.literal: Han perished.

units.zh: 自隱帝崩後四十二日，周太祖始即位，而斷自帝崩書「漢亡」者，見帝而漢崩亡矣。
units.en: Taizu of Zhou did not take the throne until forty-two days after Yindi died, but the text marks “Han perished” at the emperor’s death to show that Han fell with him.
units.literal: Forty-two days after Yindi died, Taizu of Zhou finally took the throne; yet cutting it off at the emperor’s death and writing “Han perished” shows that with the emperor Han had collapsed and perished.

units.zh: 其太后臨朝，湘陰公嗣立，皆周所假託，非誠實，所以破其姦，故書曰「漢亡」，見周之立遲也，遲而難於自立，則猶有自媿之心焉。
units.en: The empress dowager’s regency and the Duke of Xiangyin’s succession were Zhou pretexts, not realities. To expose that deceit, the text says “Han perished,” showing how slowly Zhou dared to establish itself; that delay shows it still felt some shame.
units.literal: The empress dowager’s holding court and the succession of the Duke of Xiangyin were both pretexts used by Zhou and were not sincere; to expose this deceit, it therefore writes “Han perished,” showing that Zhou’s establishment was delayed, and that in being delayed and finding it hard to establish itself, it still had some sense of shame.

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 人君即位稱元年，常事爾，古不以為重也。
units.en: For a ruler to take the throne and name the first year of his reign was routine; the ancients did not make much of it.
units.literal: When a lord takes the throne and calls it year one of his reign, it is an ordinary matter; antiquity did not treat it as weighty.

units.zh: 孔子未修《春秋》，其前固已如此，雖暴君昏主，妄庸之史，其記事先後遠近，莫不以歲月一二數之，乃理之自然也。
units.en: Even before Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn Annals the practice was fixed: tyrants and foolish kings, with incompetent scribes, still ordered events near and far by a year or two of numbering—it is simply how reason arranges things.
units.literal: Before Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn Annals it was already so; even tyrants and muddle-headed rulers, with worthless chroniclers, recorded events in near and far order, all counting by one or two year-numbers—it is the natural course of reason.

units.zh: 其謂一為元，亦未嘗有法，蓋古人之語爾。
units.en: The notion that the first year should be called the “origin” was never a binding rule—only an old way of speaking.
units.literal: That “one” should be called the origin was never really a fixed law; it is only how the ancients spoke.

units.zh: 古謂歲之一月，亦不云一，而曰正月。
units.en: In ancient usage, the first month of the year was likewise not numbered as “one”; it was called the Correct Month.
units.literal: In antiquity, the first month of the year was likewise not called the first month, but the correct month.

units.zh: 國語言六呂曰元間大呂，周易列六爻曰初九。
units.en: The Guoyu, in discussing the six pitch-pipes, uses yuan in relation to Dalu, and the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says “initial nine.”
units.literal: The Discourses of the States, speaking of the six pitch-pipes, says yuanjian Dalü; the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says initial nine.

units.zh: 大抵古人言數多不云一，不獨謂年為元也。
units.en: Broadly speaking, ancient writers often avoided saying “one” in numbering; calling the year yuan was not unique.
units.literal: In general, when ancient people spoke of numbers, they often did not say one; it was not only that they called the year yuan.

units.zh: 及後世曲學之士，始謂孔子書「元年」為《春秋》大法，遂以改元為重事。
units.en: Only later did narrow scholars decide that Confucius’s “year one” in the Spring and Autumn Annals was the classic’s grand law, and they turned the change of reign title into a solemn matter.
units.literal: Only later did pedantic scholars begin to say that Confucius’s writing of “year one” in the Spring and Autumn was the great principle of that classic, and so they made changing the reign title a weighty affair.

units.zh: 自漢以後，又名年以建元，而正偽紛雜，稱號遂多，不勝其紀也。
units.en: After Han, rulers also named their eras by “establishing the origin,” and with legitimacy and usurpation hopelessly mixed, reign titles multiplied until no one could keep track.
units.literal: From Han onward reigns were also named by “establishing the origin,” and orthodoxy and usurpation became tangled until titles multiplied beyond counting.

units.zh: 五代，亂世也，其事無法而不合於理者多矣，皆不足道也。
units.en: The Five Dynasties were a time of chaos; much that they did was lawless and unreasonable, and hardly merits discussion.
units.literal: The Five Dynasties were an age of disorder; many of their affairs lacked proper method and accorded ill with reason—they are not worth discussing.

units.zh: 至其年號乖錯以惑後世，則不可以不明。
units.en: But where their era names were twisted so as to confuse posterity, the record must be set straight.
units.literal: Yet where their reign titles were twisted and wrong and would mislead later ages, that cannot be left unclear.

units.zh: 初，梁太祖以乾化二年遇弒，明年，末帝已誅友珪，黜其鳳歷之號，復稱乾化三年，尚為有說。
units.en: When Liang Taizu was murdered in Qianhua 2, the Last Emperor the next year killed You Gui, abolished his Fengli era, and returned to Qianhua 3—one could still find a reason for that.
units.literal: At first Liang Taizu was assassinated in the second year of Qianhua; the next year the Last Emperor had You Gui executed, set aside his Fengli reign title, and restored the third year of Qianhua—there was still some rationale in that.

units.zh: 至漢高祖建國，黜晉出帝開運四年，復稱天福十二年者，何哉？
units.en: When Han Gaozu founded the dynasty, cast aside the Outgoing Emperor’s Kaiyun 4, and revived Tianfu 12—what was that for?
units.literal: But when Han Gaozu founded his state, set aside the Outgoing Emperor’s fourth Kaiyun year, and revived the twelfth Tianfu year—why?

units.zh: 蓋以其愛憎之私爾。
units.en: Nothing but private favor and spite.
units.literal: It was merely the working of private love and hate.

units.zh: 方出帝時，漢高祖居太原，常憤憤下視晉，而晉亦陽優禮之，幸而未見其隙。
units.en: Under the Outgoing Emperor, Liu Zhiyuan at Taiyuan often looked on Jin with smoldering anger, while Jin feigned courtesy toward him and, by luck, never caught him out.
units.literal: While the Outgoing Emperor still reigned, Han Gaozu held Taiyuan and often gazed down on Jin with resentment; Jin for its part treated him with outward courtesy, and by luck never found a pretext against him.

units.zh: 及契丹滅晉，漢未嘗有赴難之意。
units.en: When the Khitan overthrew Jin, Han showed not the slightest intention of riding to its aid.
units.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Han never showed the least will to go to its rescue.

units.zh: 出帝已北遷，方陽以兵聲言追之，至土門而還。
units.en: Once the Outgoing Emperor had been taken north, Han loudly claimed to be pursuing him with an army, then marched only as far as Tumen Pass and turned back.
units.literal: After the Outgoing Emperor had been moved north, Han openly made a show of pursuing him with troops, yet turned back at Tumen Pass.

units.zh: 及其即位改元，而黜開運之號，則其用心可知矣。
units.en: When he acceded and changed the era, erasing the Kaiyun name, his purpose was plain enough.
units.literal: When he took the throne and changed the era, casting aside the Kaiyun title, his intent was plain enough.

units.zh: 蓋其於出帝無復君臣之義，而幸禍以為利者，其素誌也，可勝嘆哉！
units.en: Toward the Outgoing Emperor he no longer held any bond of ruler and subject, and welcomed disaster for gain—that had been his settled mind all along. The pity of it!
units.literal: He had long since ceased to owe the Outgoing Emperor any bond of ruler and subject, and rejoiced in calamity for profit—that was his settled mind; how lamentable!

units.zh: 夫所謂有諸中必形於外者，其見於是乎！
units.en: As the saying goes, what fills the heart must show in the face—was it not plain here?
units.literal: What they call “what is within must show without”—was it not seen here!
